segments.text: This headline was just published about me in the Wall Street Journal. People called it misogynistic, but here's why I was actually happy about it. We gave them the exclusive to cover my female particle. We're collecting 14 million data points on my menstrual cycle. And this headline covers my exact motivation behind doing this particle. Female bodies are often times seen as objects of desire. Meanwhile, our biology and health is literally forgotten, dismissed, or ignored by the scientific literature. Said simply, we are easily understood as objects, and we are not

literally understood as biological beings. The data is missing. The shared language that we would use to communicate our internal experiences, I think, is in part missing because our bodies are literally uncharted by the medical world. This opinion is actually reflected in the data. Even something as simple as how does the menstrual cycle affect our biomarkers is missing in the literature. And not one person is to blame for this, it's a systemic. And so, while we can't excuse the Wall Street Journal, we can see them as part of the system itself. That gap in understanding, I think, is part of why we cannot understand the female experience collectively, and therefore

respect it and appreciate it. So, you can see how that headline is the exact motivation behind me doing the protocol. The irony is that rigid routines do not come naturally to me. I'm a creative, chaotic human being that would much rather not be doing this. But, my hope is that through uncovering new insights about what it's like to be a female, we'll have new ways of being able to communicate with the world and translate to the masculine world we live in. This will be the most quantified menstrual cycle ever, and this is just to collect baseline measurements. Once we're done with baseline, we'll then do interventions. I'll be posting all the results here, the good, the bad, what works, what fails, so that you can glean
practical insights for yourself at home.
